title: Member Handbook: The Life of a Custom Application and Field Services Plan
content:
A plan under Custom Application and Field Services is accepted for the crop year once its entry gate is met, and only an accepted plan has work released against it. An enrolment begins in applied standing; acceptance moves it to active. A plan completes when acres worked reach the acres committed and every completed pass has been billed, so a plan with an unbilled pass stays open however finished the fields look. Completion therefore rests on two things together: the committed acres worked, and every pass billed.

Acres worked under the plan are counted up as passes are completed, and where a pass is abandoned part way the acres are put back.

### Ending a plan early

The member may withdraw an application before acceptance at no charge, and may cancel the remaining work on a live plan at any time, in which case the season commitment shortfall charge is worked out on the acres not worked. Where a weather hold runs past the end of the season the cooperative cancels the remaining acres itself and the shortfall charge is waived, because the work could not be done.

### After a plan ends

Completed and cancelled are both terminal, and acres a member wants worked afterwards go onto a new plan at the day's rates. A plan never carries over into the next crop year, because the rates and the commitment are written for one season.

### The standings a plan passes through

| From | To | Moved by | What the move means |
|---|---|---|---|
| applied | active | the cooperative | the plan is accepted for the crop year and work may be released against it |
| applied | cancelled | the member | the member withdraws the plan before it is accepted |
| active | weather hold | automatically, on the records | field conditions stop work across the plan |
| weather hold | active | the cooperative | conditions clear and work resumes |
| active | completed | automatically, on the records | every committed acre has been worked and billed |
| active | cancelled | the member | the member cancels the remaining work on the plan |
| weather hold | cancelled | the cooperative | the season runs out while work is held and the remaining acres are released |

### Two illustrations on hypothetical figures

*Every acre worked, one pass unbilled.* A plan committing 500 acres has had 500 acres worked, but the last pass of 40 acres has not yet been billed. The plan does not complete, because completion asks for the committed acres worked and every pass billed, and only the first of those has happened.

*A hold that outruns the season.* A plan committing 500 acres stands under a weather hold with 120 acres still to work when the season runs out. The cooperative cancels the remaining acres itself, and no shortfall charge is raised on those 120 acres.
